comment: Shared reference-image (edit_images) expectations per model tier. The Rust test `flux2_reference_parity_fixture_pins_every_surface` in crates/mold-core/src/generation_profile.rs and the browser test studio/lib/flux2ReferenceParity.test.ts both read this file, so a drift between the server's advertised `capabilities.reference_images` and any client's presentation fails CI. Additive: new tiers join as new rows; new per-row keys join without touching existing ones. Mirrors the wan surface-parity fixture precedent (#806).

source_relation_meaning.replaces: References replace the source image; `source_image`, `mask_image`, and ControlNet inputs are refused whether or not references are attached.
source_relation_meaning.exclusive: The recipe renders from a source image OR from references, never both in one pass; the img2img fields are refused only once references are attached.

models.comment: FLUX.2 [dev]'s reference protocol replaces img2img entirely, and its loader refuses LoRA — that refusal belongs to the checkpoint, not to this block.

Distilled Klein 4B. Same checkpoint layout and same t = 10 + 10*i reference ids as [dev] (diffusers pipeline_flux2_klein.py:318-366 is 'Copied from' pipeline_flux2.py), but Klein keeps img2img, the inpainting mask, and LoRA — so a request carries one form or the other.
Undistilled Klein base 9B: architecturally identical, sampled with real CFG. The reference contract is a family property, not a tier property.

The FIRST image is the edit target, which is why this recipe's canvas is source-driven and its source ceiling is the reference ceiling. The only tier that cannot render without one. No count ceiling of its own; 1-3 images is upstream advice, not a bound.
FLUX.1 [dev] has no reference protocol today (Kontext is a separate checkpoint, filed as its own PR). A hidden block is the control's absence with a sentence attached, never a client-side guess.
